svg.title: The publish flow, the two proofs it checks, and the same flow inside CI
svg.desc: Five command boxes run left to right: init, validate, login, publish, status, with the publish box filled in terracotta because it is the step the figure is about, and a note that status is the only lever you have afterwards. A line drops from publish onto a single horizontal rail, labelled one moment two checks, and two equal arms come off that rail into two panels of identical size. Panel one is namespace ownership, proved by a GitHub login granting your io.github namespace, a DNS TXT record beginning v=MCPv1, or a file served at /.well-known/mcp-registry-auth on your own domain, with a note that Ed25519 keys are 64 hex characters and P-384 keys are 96. Panel two is ownership of the package the entry points at, proved by a marker inside the package itself: an HTML comment in the README for PyPI, an mcpName property in package.json for npm, and for an MCPB bundle a file hash on a GitHub or GitLab release, with a note that this proof lives inside the package rather than in the command line tool, and that missing it fails with Registry validation failed for package. Below, two boxes show the same flow in continuous integration: a workflow needing only the id-token write permission and a login github-oidc line, with no stored secret, and a panel noting that OIDC grants the repository owner's namespace rather than the pushing user's and that the audience claim is derived from the registry URL, so an old publisher fails with invalid audience and the fix is to upgrade it. A closing line says the top-level version and the package version must move together.
svg.text: Five commands, and the two proofs behind the fourth
Publish the package first and the registry entry second. The registry checks the artifact exists.
Ed25519 keys are 64 hex characters; P-384 keys are 96.
you own the package it points at
mcpb mcpb + fileSha256, on a github or gitlab release
This one lives inside the package, not in the CLI.
Missing the second one fails with "Registry validation failed for package".
The same flow in continuous integration, with nothing stored
id-token: write # the whole secret story
The interactive device code, replaced by a token minted for the job.
OIDC grants the repository owner's namespace, not the pusher's.
aud is derived from --registry, so an old publisher fails
with "invalid audience". Upgrade it, not your workflow.
Bump version and packages[].version together, or the registry advertises a release that is not on PyPI yet.
